limitations: Printed p.38 (PDF p.46) reports monitored pressure 99.2–99.5 kPa for its test subset; printed p.94 (PDF p.102) gives ambient pressure 1 atm and Kanthal hot-wire ignition for another subset.
Printed p.11 (PDF p.19) uses 1 atm and 300 K in a gas-law calculation; these are calculation inputs, not per-test measurements.
No row-level pressure or ignition-method mapping was verified; normalized record fields remain null. Report contains findings beyond the two ingested CSVs.

claims.claim_text: BASS-II studied ignition, flame growth, flame spread and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity.
claims.limitation: Investigation-level objective, not a per-test result.

claims.claim_text: BASS-II used a small wind tunnel in the Microgravity Science Glovebox with airflow speeds up to 40 cm/s; oxygen was varied by nitrogen vitiation.
claims.limitation: Describes the investigation approach, not the actual setting of every test.

claims.claim_text: The BASS-II oxygen sensor was out of calibration; the initial ISS air reading was corrected using the MCA ISS reading via a constant offset.
supporting_locators: PSI-25 ReadMe, 'Calibrated initial and final O2'
claims.limitation: A constant-offset correction is a documented approximation; per-sample uncertainty is not supplied.

claims.claim_text: The BASS-II 'Air display' is a duct flow-speed display in cm/s with a response time of about one minute; it is only steady for long holds at one setting.
claims.limitation: Values recorded during ramps or short holds should not be treated as steady calibrated velocities.

claims.claim_text: The BASS-II 'Fan display' is an instantaneous fan voltage times ten, not a flow velocity.
claims.limitation: Fan display must not be converted directly to velocity; use the separate air display and calibration.

claims.claim_text: The PSI-25 fan-calibration workbook gives U = 1.0066 x Air display, based on SPICE fan calibration at 56 mm downstream and 36 mm from the bottom (centerline).
supporting_locators: PSI-25 Fan Calibration data sheet, note '*U =1.0066(AIR)'
claims.limitation: A single factor is an approximation; day- and restrictor-specific calibration exists and per-test calibration was not applied.

claims.claim_text: Saffire-I and Saffire-III used SIBAL cloth, a 75% cotton / 25% fiberglass composite fabric, at a nominal air-flow velocity of 20 cm/s for Saffire-I.
claims.limitation: Material and nominal flow are investigation-level descriptions; the per-sample table reports 20 cm/s for both S1 and S2.

claims.claim_text: LUCI demonstrated material flammability experiments in simulated lunar gravity on a spinning Blue Origin New Shepard, at 11 RPM with an effective radius of 1.22 m; the burn lasted more than two and a half minutes.
claims.limitation: LUCI is context, not part of the PSI experiment corpus; no structured per-test records were imported.

claims.claim_text: In the LUCI lunar-g burn, SIBAL flame base spread was 0.92 mm/s and flame tip spread 1.1 mm/s; PMMA flame tip spread was about 1.5 mm/s, and chamber O2 fell from 20% to 14.3%.
claims.limitation: Presentation-level findings from a single LUCI flight; not reproduced here and not directly comparable to BASS-II/Saffire records.

claims.claim_text: The official 2026 challenge states that there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI, and that LUCI and FM2 data are expected in the future.
claims.limitation: This describes PSI's public corpus at the time of the challenge; it is not a claim that no partial-gravity research exists anywhere.

claims.claim_text: The BASS-II experimental table does not report total pressure, so oxygen partial pressure cannot be calculated at record level from this table alone.
claims.limitation: Absence of a pressure column is not evidence that pressure was unmeasured or uncontrolled; it is a metadata gap.

claims.claim_text: The Saffire-I experimental table does not report total pressure, so oxygen partial pressure cannot be calculated at record level from this table alone.
claims.limitation: Absence of a pressure column is not evidence that pressure was unmeasured or uncontrolled; it is a metadata gap.

presets.label: Earth sea level
presets.description: Standard dry-air oxygen fraction at NASA's stated sea-level pressure.
presets.source: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge text (14.7 psi); NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet (20.95% O2 by volume).
presets.caveat: Reference atmosphere, not an experiment in the corpus.

presets.label: Spacesuit (100% O2)
presets.description: Spacesuits are filled with 100% oxygen to 4.3 psi to enable flexibility.
presets.source: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge text, 'Spacesuits and oxygen concentration'.
presets.caveat: Reference scenario stated in the challenge; not a per-test experimental condition in this corpus.

presets.label: Lunar cabin planning point
presets.description: Illustrative point at the challenge's stated upper-bound planning values: 30% O2 or greater, 10.2 psi or less.
presets.source: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge text, 'Spacesuits and oxygen concentration'.
presets.caveat: Illustrative planning point derived from the challenge text. It is not a final operational specification for a Moon Base or rover.

limitations: The current corpus contains BASS-II (129 records) and Saffire-I (2 records). It is not the whole of NASA combustion research.
Total pressure is absent from both PSI experimental tables; no cabin pressure was substituted.
Gravity is investigation-level only (ISS/Cygnus microgravity), not a per-test measured g-level.
Neither table contains a standardized extinction/sustained-burning outcome.
BASS-II flow values are slow-response displays; Saffire-I reports a setting. The BASS-II derived velocity uses one factor, not a per-test calibration.
O2 readings were corrected by a constant offset because the sensor was out of calibration; per-sample uncertainty is not supplied.
Material family, geometry and dimensions are parsed from free-text fields and marked derived.
Two BASS-II final-O2 values exceed their initial values by more than 2 percentage points and are flagged suspect, not corrected.
No partial-gravity experiment records are included. The official challenge states PSI currently has none; LUCI is included only as context.
No AI-generated scientific claims are presented. The evidence assistant is a deterministic retrieval and citation engine.
